content.content: {"result":"{\"documentId\": \"f_3ca9e15d7b20f4e681ad52\", \"title\": \"DD bug carry-over notes\", \"name\": \"DD bug carry-over notes\", \"revisionId\": \"42599f1a8a\", \"createdTime\": \"2026-02-12T22:48:00Z\", \"modifiedTime\": \"2026-02-12T22:48:00Z\", \"text\": \"DD bug carry-over notes\\n\\nWhat goes over: every ticked or unticked line in the comment channel of Vincent's Android canvas, and every bug posted in the bug channel after the last line in that comment channel. A comment whose line was deleted has nothing to carry over. In the bug channel a follow-up on a bug already posted is part of that bug, and a design question for Leonard or a post that points at a QA doc isn't a bug post. Nothing else. Robert's reports in the sub-250 channel aren't part of this, Brian dealt with those at the time. The economy canvas and the ZM canvases stay where they are.\\n\\nOne Linear record per canvas line and one per bug posted after it. A canvas line and a later post stay separate even where they read alike. Take the first outcome that fits.\\nFixed: the tick stands, or a later record says it was fixed. File it as Done.\\nGone: it isn't fixed and it's a bug in something the build players have no longer has. File it as Canceled.\\nCovered: it isn't fixed and an open ticket already covers it. Don't file a new one, add a note on that ticket with the canvas wording. Vincent tied a few lines to tickets before he left.\\nBroken: anything else. File it as Bugs.\\n\\nWhat counts: we go by the Android build players have, 0.3.310, which came off the economy line, not by develop. A tick on the canvas stands unless a later record about that bug says otherwise. An unticked line, or a bug nobody closed, stays open unless a later record says it was fixed, and a commit named for the bug counts as that record if nothing later says otherwise. A fix only counts once it is in that build. A PR that never made it into that build doesn't count.\\n\\nNew tickets: Engineering team, Bug label, parent ENG-2401, title is the line without its tick box, or the first line of the post, as it was written, no assignee, nothing in the description. If anything changes after this I'll put it on the master ticket.\\n\\nUI tree: every open child goes Done unless a record shows a piece of its UI work never made it into that build or the screen is switched off there. Then it stays where it is. Children already Done stay Done and the masters stay as they are. A bug on a screen doesn't hold its child, that's what the bug ticket is for. Brian and Oliver left notes on some of the open children. Brian's closing rule from the UI work applies to the line on every child, Done or not.\\n\\nSheet columns: Bug, Outcome, Ticket, Why. When you report back, Covered ones count as still broken.\\n\"}"}

{"documentId": "f_3ca9e15d7b20f4e681ad52", "title": "DD bug carry-over notes", "name": "DD bug carry-over notes", "revisionId": "42599f1a8a", "createdTime": "2026-02-12T22:48:00Z", "modifiedTime": "2026-02-12T22:48:00Z", "text": "DD bug carry-over notes

What goes over: every ticked or unticked line in the comment channel of Vincent's Android canvas, and every bug posted in the bug channel after the last line in that comment channel. A comment whose line was deleted has nothing to carry over. In the bug channel a follow-up on a bug already posted is part of that bug, and a design question for Leonard or a post that points at a QA doc isn't a bug post. Nothing else. Robert's reports in the sub-250 channel aren't part of this, Brian dealt with those at the time. The economy canvas and the ZM canvases stay where they are.

One Linear record per canvas line and one per bug posted after it. A canvas line and a later post stay separate even where they read alike. Take the first outcome that fits.
Fixed: the tick stands, or a later record says it was fixed. File it as Done.
Gone: it isn't fixed and it's a bug in something the build players have no longer has. File it as Canceled.
Covered: it isn't fixed and an open ticket already covers it. Don't file a new one, add a note on that ticket with the canvas wording. Vincent tied a few lines to tickets before he left.
Broken: anything else. File it as Bugs.

What counts: we go by the Android build players have, 0.3.310, which came off the economy line, not by develop. A tick on the canvas stands unless a later record about that bug says otherwise. An unticked line, or a bug nobody closed, stays open unless a later record says it was fixed, and a commit named for the bug counts as that record if nothing later says otherwise. A fix only counts once it is in that build. A PR that never made it into that build doesn't count.

New tickets: Engineering team, Bug label, parent ENG-2401, title is the line without its tick box, or the first line of the post, as it was written, no assignee, nothing in the description. If anything changes after this I'll put it on the master ticket.

UI tree: every open child goes Done unless a record shows a piece of its UI work never made it into that build or the screen is switched off there. Then it stays where it is. Children already Done stay Done and the masters stay as they are. A bug on a screen doesn't hold its child, that's what the bug ticket is for. Brian and Oliver left notes on some of the open children. Brian's closing rule from the UI work applies to the line on every child, Done or not.

Sheet columns: Bug, Outcome, Ticket, Why. When you report back, Covered ones count as still broken.
"}

orph=[k for k in reps if k not in seen]
print('orphans',orph)
EOF

Camera-based UI is affected by URP changes\nWhen the Canvas is set to *Screen Space \u2013 Camera* (or World Space):\n\u2022 UI is rendered *by a Camera*\n\u2022 It goes through the *same render pipeline as the 3D scene*\n\u2022 Disabling *lighting, shadows, or post-processing* changes the camera\u2019s render path\n\u2022 On some Android GPUs, this causes the UI to:\nNot render at all, or\nRender incorrectly (z-order / alpha / depth issues)\nThis is why the bottom bar disappears *only after lighting/shadow changes*.\n\n2. Screen Space \u2013 Overlay fixes UI, but exposes another dependency\nWhen switching to *Screen Space \u2013 Overlay*:\n\u2022 UI is rendered *after the scene*\n\u2022 It bypasses:\nCameras\nLighting\nShadows\nPost-processing\nSo the bottom bar becomes visible again.\nHowever, this also *removes any implicit coupling* between UI and the scene.\n If gameplay visuals (e.g. characters) were *incorrectly relying on camera settings shared with UI*, those issues become visible immediately.\nIn other words:\n> Overlay mode didn\u2019t break character visuals \u2014 it *revealed an existing dependency*.\n3. Why this happens only on some Android devices\nDifferent Android devices use different GPUs (Adreno, Mali, PowerVR), and:\n\u2022 They handle *depth, alpha, and render order* differently\n\u2022 URP shader variants and render passes can behave inconsistently\n\u2022 Some devices fail silently instead of logging errors\nThis is why:\n\u2022 The issue does not reproduce on all devices\n\u2022 It appears specifically after lighting/shadow changes\nKey Takeaway\nThe core problem is *not the UI itself*, but that:\n> *UI and gameplay rendering are incorrectly coupled through the same camera / render pipeline.*\nScreen Space \u2013 Overlay is a *valid fix for UI*, but the character rendering issue indicates *another underlying render dependency* that needs to be separated.", "channel":       This issue is caused by a *mix of UI render mode, URP rendering behavior, and device-specific GPU differences*.

      • UI is rendered *after the scene*
      • It bypasses:

      Shadows
      Post-processing
      So the bottom bar becomes visible again.
      However, this also *removes any implicit coupling* between UI and the scene.

      • They handle *depth, alpha, and render order* differently

*First Batch*
We subtract ~1000 coins locally for the ticket purchase
We add 1 ticket locally

*Second Batch*

{"ts": "1764658511.920629", "type": "message", "text": "1. **Replace lives with tickets**

* Implement tickets as the new entry currency: 1 ticket or 1 000 coins or timed infinite ticket to play.
* Add 3 play button states (coins, ticket count, timed infinite).
* Remove lives from HUD, minigames, rewards, shop, season pass, Nate, quests, FTUE, and out-of-lives flow.
* Introduce tickets in daily/weekly chests and the new FTUE quest.

2. **Make the game harder**

* Nerf [PERSON_NAME_3999]’s Favor so it gives fewer tiles and coins.

3. **Rebalance rewards**

* Update event and LiveOps reward tables to reduce free boosters, remove infinite lives, and add some ticket or gem rewards where specified.

4. **Tighten coin and upgrade economy**

* Switch character upgrades from coins to gems using the new gem cost table.
* Keep coins focused on level entry.

5. **Dynamic difficulty**

"message", "text": "Why This Issue Is Happening (Root Cause)
This issue is caused by a *mix of UI render mode, URP rendering behavior, and device-specific GPU differences*.
1. Camera-based UI is affected by URP changes
When the Canvas is set to *Screen Space – Camera* (or World Space):
• UI is rendered *by a Camera*
• It goes through the *same render pipeline as the 3D scene*
• Disabling *lighting, shadows, or post-processing* changes the camera’s render path
• On some Android GPUs, this causes the UI to:
Not render at all, or
Render incorrectly (z-order / alpha / depth issues)
This is why the bottom bar disappears *only after lighting/shadow changes*.

2. Screen Space – Overlay fixes UI, but exposes another dependency
When switching to *Screen Space – Overlay*:
• UI is rendered *after the scene*
• It bypasses:
Cameras
Lighting
Shadows
Post-processing
So the bottom bar becomes visible again.
However, this also *removes any implicit coupling* between UI and the scene.
 If gameplay visuals (e.g. characters) were *incorrectly relying on camera settings shared with UI*, those issues become visible immediately.
In other words:
> Overlay mode didn’t break character visuals — it *revealed an existing dependency*.
3. Why this happens only on some Android devices
Different Android devices use different GPUs (Adreno, Mali, PowerVR), and:
• They handle *depth, alpha, and render order* differently
• URP shader variants and render passes can behave inconsistently
• Some devices fail silently instead of logging errors
This is why:
• The issue does not reproduce on all devices
• It appears specifically after lighting/shadow changes
Key Takeaway
The core problem is *not the UI itself*, but that:
> *UI and gameplay rendering are incorrectly coupled through the same camera / render pipeline.*
Screen Space – Overlay is a *valid fix for UI*, but the character rendering issue indicates *another underlying render dependency* that needs to be separated.", "channel": "C05V5FNLB9V", "user": "EMPLOYEE_0026_SLACK_ID", "thread_ts": "1766415326.501939", "channel_info": {"id": "C05V5FNLB9V", "name": "god-bugs", "is_private": true, "is_im": false, "is_mpim": false}, "user_profile": {"id": "EMPLOYEE_0026_SLACK_ID", "name": "Brian Foster", "real_name": "Brian Foster", "display_name": "Brian Foster", "email": "brian.foster@harmonygames.co"}, "time": "2025-12-22T15:16:29Z", "permalink": "https://harmonygamesgroup.slack.com/archives/C05V5FNLB9V/p1766416589444619?thread_ts=1766415326.501939&cid=C05V5FNLB9V"}, {"ts": "1766416568.655679", "type": "message", "text": "I don’t fully understand it either, but this is how chatgpt explains the issue, and changing the render mode fixes it. content.content: {"result":"{\"ok\": true, \"messages\": [{\"ts\": \"1769892718.932069\", \"type\": \"message\", \"text\": \"Simple improvement: Upgrade-adjusted difficulty multiplier (plus a tiny \\u201cskill\\u201d correction)\\nKeep your current per-level curve, but apply a multiplier based on how far a player\\u2019s upgrades are above or below the expected upgrade curve for that level. This directly addresses \\u201cahead early, stays ahead for 10+ levels.\\u201d\\n1) Compute an upgrade power score\\nUse what you already have (HP, Regen, Attack upgrades). Start linear.\\n\\u2022 `U = 0.4 * HP + 0.3 * Regen + 0.3 * Attack`\\n(Adjust weights later if Attack dominates outcomes, but start here.)\\n2) Maintain an expected upgrade curve by level\\nYou need `E[level] = expected U at this level` from either:\\ndesign intent (a table), or\\n\\u2022 median `U` from live data per level (better once you have enough data).\\n3) Convert \\u201cahead/behind\\u201d into a difficulty multiplier\\n\\u2022 `delta = U - E[level]`\\n\\u2022 `M_upg = clamp(1 + k * delta, 0.85, 1.25)`\\nWhere `k` is small (start `k = 0.05`).\\nExample using your comment \\u201c3 to 4 levels ahead\\u201d: if that maps to `delta = +2`, then `M_upg = 1.10`. That is enough to pull you back into \\u201cneed to think\\u201d without nuking average players.\\n4) Optional, still simple: a 3-bucket \\u201cskill\\u201d correction\\nThis keeps the fully-upgraded-but-crappy player from getting obliterated instantly, while still letting them struggle.\\nDefine `S` from the last 3 to 5 levels using only cheap telemetry:\\n\\u2022 attempts per level\\n\\u2022 time to clear\\n\\u2022 waves reached at death (if you have it)\\n\\u2022 number of refreshes (if relevant)\\nBucket it:\\n\\u2022 *Strong*: low attempts, fast clears\\n\\u2022 *Average*: middle\\n\\u2022 *Weak*: high attempts, slow clears\\nThen:\\n\\u2022 `M_skill = {Strong: 1.05, Average: 1.00, Weak: 0.95}`\\nFinal:\\n\\u2022 `M = M_upg * M_skill` (still clamped to 0.85 to 1.25)\\n5) Apply M to a small set of knobs only\\nDo not touch everything. Start linear.\\n\\u2022 `U = 0.4 * HP + 0.3 * Regen + 0.3 * Attack`\\n(Adjust weights later if Attack dominates outcomes, but start here.)\\n2) Maintain an expected upgrade curve by level\\nYou need `E[level] = expected U at this level` from either:\\ndesign intent (a table), or\\n\\u2022 median `U` from live data per level (better once you have enough data).\\n3) Convert \\u201cahead/behind\\u201d into a difficulty multiplier\\n\\u2022 `delta = U - E[level]`\\n\\u2022 `M_upg = clamp(1 + k * delta, 0.85, 1.25)`\\nWhere `k` is small (start `k = 0.05`).\\nExample using your comment \\u201c3 to 4 levels ahead\\u201d: if that maps to `delta = +2`, then `M_upg = 1.10`. That is enough to pull you back into \\u201cneed to think\\u201d without nuking average players.\\n4) Optional, still simple: a 3-bucket \\u201cskill\\u201d correction\\nThis keeps the fully-upgraded-but-crappy player from getting obliterated instantly, while still letting them struggle.\\nDefine `S` from the last 3 to 5 levels using only cheap telemetry:\\n\\u2022 attempts per level\\n\\u2022 time to clear\\n\\u2022 waves reached at death (if you have it)\\n\\u2022 number of refreshes (if relevant)\\nBucket it:\\n\\u2022 *Strong*: low attempts, fast clears\\n\\u2022 *Average*: middle\\n\\u2022 *Weak*: high attempts, slow clears\\nThen:\\n\\u2022 `M_skill = {Strong: 1.05, Average: 1.00, Weak: 0.95}`\\nFinal:\\n\\u2022 `M = M_upg * M_skill` (still clamped to 0.85 to 1.25)\\n5) Apply M to a small set of knobs only\\nDo not touch everything. Pick 2 to 3 levers that reliably create \\u201cI have to rebuild now\\u201d moments.\\nGood candidates:\\n\\u2022 enemy HP (or base health pool per wave)\\n\\u2022 enemy damage (or time-to-death pressure)\\n\\u2022 obstacle density or obstacle removal cost\\n\\u2022 shape pool entropy (only if it is a main difficulty driver, and you can change it safely)\\nExample:\\n\\u2022 `EnemyHP = BaseEnemyHP(level, wave) * M`\\n\\u2022 `EnemyDPS = BaseEnemyDPS(level, wave) * (0.5 + 0.5*M)`\\n(less aggressive than HP if DPS spikes feel unfair)\\nA/B test design\\n*Control (A)*: current level-based curve.\\n*Variant (B)*: same curve times `M` (upgrade-adjusted, plus optional skill bucket).\\nPrimary success criteria (pick 2 to avoid overfitting):\\n\\u2022 level completion rate and attempts distribution (especially levels 10 to 25)\\n\\u2022 time per level and \\u201crebuild events\\u201d frequency proxy (big board changes, silver spend spikes, obstacle removals)\\n\\u2022 D1 and D3 retention (segmented by payer vs non-payer, and by upgrade delta buckets)\\nKey segmentation to validate the exact argument in your thread:\\n\\u2022 `delta >= +2` (ahead of curve, your \\u201cspender/optimizer\\u201d proxy)\\n\\u2022 `delta between -1 and +1` (on-curve average)\\n\\u2022 `delta <= -2` (behind curve)\\nExpected outcome if this works:\\n\\u2022 ahead-of-curve players stop cruising for 10 levels, they hit meaningful rebuilds earlier (around level 11 to 12 if that\\u2019s your target)\\n\\u2022 average players stay near current difficulty\\n\\u2022 weak players still struggle, but not catastrophically earlier than today (your existing retry-based adjustments can remain as the safety net)\\nIf you want the minimum possible engineering change: implement only `M_upg` with a clamped multiplier, apply it to enemy HP only, ship the A/B. 2) Maintain an expected upgrade curve by level
You need `E[level] = expected U at this level` from either:
design intent (a table), or
• median `U` from live data per level (better once you have enough data).
3) Convert “ahead/behind” into a difficulty multiplier
• `delta = U - E[level]`
• `M_upg = clamp(1 + k * delta, 0.85, 1.25)`
Where `k` is small (start `k = 0.05`).
Example using your comment “3 to 4 levels ahead”: if that maps to `delta = +2`, then `M_upg = 1.10`. That is enough to pull you back into “need to think” without nuking average players.
4) Optional, still simple: a 3-bucket “skill” correction
This keeps the fully-upgraded-but-crappy player from getting obliterated instantly, while still letting them struggle.
Define `S` from the last 3 to 5 levels using only cheap telemetry:
• attempts per level
• time to clear
• waves reached at death (if you have it)
• number of refreshes (if relevant)
Bucket it:
• *Strong*: low attempts, fast clears
• *Average*: middle
• *Weak*: high attempts, slow clears
Then:
• `M_skill = {Strong: 1.05, Average: 1.00, Weak: 0.95}`
Final:
• `M = M_upg * M_skill` (still clamped to 0.85 to 1.25)
5) Apply M to a small set of knobs only
Do not touch everything. Pick 2 to 3 levers that reliably create “I have to rebuild now” moments.
Good candidates:
• enemy HP (or base health pool per wave)
• enemy damage (or time-to-death pressure)
• obstacle density or obstacle removal cost
• shape pool entropy (only if it is a main difficulty driver, and you can change it safely)
Example:
• `EnemyHP = BaseEnemyHP(level, wave) * M`
• `EnemyDPS = BaseEnemyDPS(level, wave) * (0.5 + 0.5*M)`
(less aggressive than HP if DPS spikes feel unfair)
A/B test design
*Control (A)*: current level-based curve.
*Variant (B)*: same curve times `M` (upgrade-adjusted, plus optional skill bucket).
Primary success criteria (pick 2 to avoid overfitting):
• level completion rate and attempts distribution (especially levels 10 to 25)
• time per level and “rebuild events” frequency proxy (big board changes, silver spend spikes, obstacle removals)
• D1 and D3 retention (segmented by payer vs non-payer, and by upgrade delta buckets)
Key segmentation to validate the exact argument in your thread:
• `delta >= +2` (ahead of curve, your “spender/optimizer” proxy)
• `delta between -1 and +1` (on-curve average)
• `delta <= -2` (behind curve)
Expected outcome if this works:
• ahead-of-curve players stop cruising for 10 levels, they hit meaningful rebuilds earlier (around level 11 to 12 if that’s your target)
• average players stay near current difficulty
• weak players still struggle, but not catastrophically earlier than today (your existing retry-based adjustments can remain as the safety net)
If you want the minimum possible engineering change: implement only `M_upg` with a clamped multiplier, apply it to enemy HP only, ship the A/B. {"result":"{\"id\": \"page_qa_runbook\", \"space_id\": \"space_ENG\", \"parent_id\": \"page_eng_home\", \"title\": \"QA Regression Runbook\", \"body\": \"

Manual QA regression pass run against every release candidate before we submit a build for review. Last owned by QA (Arthur Blake, who took it over from Vincent Parker when Vincent Parker left in Nov 2025; Arthur Blake stayed through the February 2026 wind-down); anyone cutting a build can run it, but a green matrix here is a gate on the Release Checklist & Store Submission. Scope covers Domino Delights (internal codename GoD, \\\"Game of Dominoes\\\"), Zombie Match 3D (listed as \\\"Puzzles vs Zombies\\\" until the July 2025 rename) and Combo Fighter. Androidcurrent-gen Samsung / Pixellow-RAM device, oldest supported OSone Android tablet
\\n

"https://harmonygamesgroup.slack.com/archives/C09UHHN6PFZ/p1769038533784879?thread_ts=1769033022.034089&cid=C09UHHN6PFZ"}, {"ts": "1769037874.532759", "type": "message", "text": "Here is the same analysis using *all lost attempts in the “no missing fields” export*.
Dataset
• *18 lost attempts* (App versions: *1.0.56 = 15*, *1.0.57 = 3*)
• All rows have the key gameplay fields populated.
Do losers buy pieces?
Yes, always.
*18/18 (100%)* bought pieces.
• Pieces bought distribution: *median 7*, p25 *5.25*, p75 *9*, range *2–12*.
Takeaway: “they aren’t buying” is not the issue.

Do losers sell pieces?
Rarely (for actual tiles).
• *Tiles Sold Int > 0:* *6/18 (33%)*
Tiles sold: median *0*, p75 *1*, max *9*.
• *Trash Sold Int > 0:* *18/18 (100%)*
Trash sold: median *8*, range *2–18*.
Takeaway: if “selling tiles” is a core mechanic, adoption is low. Trash selling looks universal, so either it is easy/automatic, or it is the only “sell” behavior players understand.

Do losers remove obstacles?
Yes, always.
*Obstacles Removed Int > 0:* *18/18 (100%)*
• Obstacles removed: *median 4*, p75 *6*, range *1–7*.
Takeaway: “they aren’t removing obstacles” is not supported by this dataset.

Do losers build combos?
You still do not log combos directly, but *Highest Dps Int* is your best proxy.
• Highest DPS: *median 508.5*, p75 *621*, max *1189*.
Takeaway: many losing runs ramp to substantial DPS, especially in late deaths, so a large part of the problem is not “no combos,” it is “combos not enough to survive the late curve” or “spend not converting to survivability.”

What does Silver Balance Int tell us?
Everyone dies with silver left.
• *Silver Balance Int*: median *84*, p75 *108*, max *160*, min *38*.
Takeaway: players are not ending at “0 resources.” They are dying with spendable currency still in hand, which usually points to one of:
1. spend options are not impactful enough to change outcomes,
2. shop decisions are unclear (players buy the wrong things),
3. shop timing/UX friction (they do not spend at the right moment).
How behavior changes by where they die
Segmented by *Highest Wave Reached Int*:
Early deaths (<= 6), N=4
Pieces bought median *4.5*
Obstacles removed median *2*
DPS median *178*
Silver median *67*
• Tiles sold any *25%*
Interpretation: these are “didn’t ramp” runs, likely skill/understanding + early variance.
Mid deaths (7–9), N=4
Pieces bought median *6*
Obstacles removed median *4.5*
DPS median *376.5*
Silver median *71*
• Tiles sold any *50%* (highest of the three groups)
Interpretation: midgame wall starts showing, some players try selling as a recovery move.
Late deaths (>= 10), N=10
Pieces bought median *9*
Obstacles removed median *5.5*
DPS median *611*
Silver median *107*
• Tiles sold any *30%*
Interpretation: late losers are actively playing the systems (buying, clearing, ramping DPS) and still die, often with meaningful silver left. That is tuning plus spend-impact, not “they didn’t engage.”

What you should change (based on this)
If you want win rate to move hard, focus on two things.
1) Make spending convert into survival
You have clear evidence of “dies with silver left,” especially in late runs.
Add *recommended purchase* (one button) when HP is low or wave >= 10 and silver >= X.
• Add *auto-open shop* at wave checkpoints (ex: after wave 6 and wave 10) with 1–2 highlighted options.
• Buff the best defensive/sustain option so it reliably prevents late deaths (shield, lifesteal, regen spike, damage reduction).
2) Decide whether tile-selling is supposed to matter
Because Tiles Sold is only *33%*:
• If selling is intended core: force it in FTUE once, and add a contextual prompt when the board is tight (“sell lowest value tile” preselected).
• If selling is optional: stop assuming it is the reason for losses, and tune the level assuming most players will not sell tiles.
One logging gap to close
To prove your theory cleanly, you need:
• *Silver spent total* and *purchase types* (offense vs defense vs utility), plus *time since last purchase*.
Right now you only know they _bought some pieces_ and _had silver left_. You cannot tell whether they failed because they did not spend, or because they spent on weak/wrong things.

## 🧩 **Endless Mode – Engineering Summary**

### 🔧 Initial Setup

- Game starts with **40–45 sets** (a set = 3 items).
- **8 unique item types**, with size distribution:
  - 2 Large, 4 medium, 2 Small.
- Entire **item pool is defined by the designer** for each endless variant.
- Monsters also follow **30-second "tracks"**, authored by designers using level editor tools.

---

### 🔄 Refill System (Every 30 seconds)

1. **Track matched items** from the last 30 seconds.
2. **Refill those exact items** to keep total set count at 40–45.
3. Each refill is simulated and checked against a **growing Unique Item Cap**:

Refill #Time (s)Unique Cap130826093909412010.........1236014

---

### 🧠 Refill Logic Rules

1. **Simulate a refill**: Replace all matched items 1:1.
2. **Count unique items** on the new board.
3. If unique count is **below cap**:
   - Attempt to **substitute refilled items** with new unique items one-by-one.
   - After each substitution, re-check unique count.
4. If still short:
   - Remove a **fraction of total sets** = `#missingUniques / targetUniqueCap`.
   - Replace them with random sets using new unique items to reach the cap.

**Key principle:** Total number of sets never changes; only uniqueness does.

---

### 💥 New Mechanic: The Nuke (Replaces Boss Buster)

- **Builds power** by matching items:
  `NukePower += itemAttackPower × 10% × comboMultiplier`
- **Combo System**:
  - Starts at **1x**.
  - Combo meter fills after each match and **decays** over time.
  - If matched before timeout, combo increases.
  - Decay window shrinks by 0.25s each level (starts at 4.5s).
  - Max achievable combo: 18x.
  - The **next match** receives the combo multiplier shown.

ComboTimeout2x4.5s3x4.25s......18x~0s

- **Minimum power to activate Nuke** = 50.

cd /home/agent/.claude/projects/-app/4c4556d9-0164-41b3-8ef9-c629c9d14ec8/tool-results/; python3 - <<'EOF'
import json
ms=[]
for f in ['mcp-hg-slack_conversations_search_messages-1794090799907.txt','mcp-hg-slack_conversations_search_messages-1794090810422.txt','mcp-hg-slack_conversations_search_messages-1794090819571.txt']:
  ms+=json.loads(json.load(open(f))['result'])['messages']
seen={m['ts']:m for m in ms}
roots=sorted([m for m in seen.values() if m.get('subtype')=='document_comment_root' and m['text'].strip()],key=lambda m:float(m['ts']))
out=[]
for i,r in enumerate(roots,1):
  t=r['text']
  tick=t[0]
  body=t[1:].strip()
  out.append({'n':i,'ts':r['ts'],'tick':'ticked' if tick=='☑' else 'unticked','text':body})
print(len(out))
json.dump(out,open('/tmp/canvas_lines.json','w'),indent=0,ensure_ascii=False)
for o in out: print(o['n'],o['tick'],repr(o['text']))
EOF

content.text:
This session is being continued from a previous conversation that ran out of context. The summary below covers the earlier portion of the conversation.

Summary:
1. Primary Request and Intent:
   Owen asked me to do what Arthur Blake laid out in his DM (D05S1S2AB5M, ts 1770937805.214409, Feb 12), all before Sunday's bug review:
   - Move DD's bug list from Slack into Linear, the fixed ones included.
   - Bring the UI Changes tree under ENG-2401 up to date and leave a line on every child saying where it landed.
   - Put a sheet in Owen's "DD bug carry-over" Drive folder (d_9b41e7c2a05d36f8e1c7a4) and share it with everyone on Sunday's bug review.
   - Reply in the DM thread with three numbers: how many are still broken, how many new tickets were filed, and how many of the 28 UI children are Done.

   **Rules from Arthur's "DD bug carry-over notes" doc (f_3ca9e15d7b20f4e681ad52):**
   - What goes over: every ticked or unticked line in the comment channel of Vincent's Android canvas (CE156FDFB428), plus every bug posted in the bug channel (#god-bugs, C05V5FNLB9V) after the last canvas line (Nov 21 15:04).
   - Lines whose text was deleted (empty comment roots) carry nothing over.
   - Follow-ups belong to the bug they follow. Design questions and QA-doc pointers are not bug posts.
   - Excluded: Robert's sub-250 reports, the economy canvas, and the ZM canvases.
   - One Linear record per line or post. Take the first outcome that fits:
     - Fixed → Done
     - Gone (feature no longer in the build) → Canceled
     - Covered by an open ticket → no new ticket; add a note on that ticket with the canvas wording
     - Broken → Bugs
   - Judge everything against Android build 0.3.310, which came off the economy line. Ticks stand unless a later record says otherwise. A commit named for the bug counts as a fix record, but only if it is in that build.
   - New tickets: Engineering team, Bug label, parent ENG-2401, no assignee, no description. Title is the line without its tick box (or the first line of the post), as written.
   - Arthur's comment on ENG-2401 adds: put "[2231] " at the front of every title.
   - UI tree: every open child goes Done, unless a record shows a piece of its UI work never made it into 0.3.310 or the screen is switched off there. Children already Done stay Done. The masters (ENG-2403/2404/2405) stay as they are.
   - Brian's closing rule applies to the line on every child, Done or not. It's in a Trello comment on the "UI optimization pass" card: "When we close these UI tickets out every one gets a note naming the current public build, otherwise nobody can tell later what players actually had."
   - Sheet columns: Bug, Outcome, Ticket, Why.
   - When reporting, count Covered as still broken.

2. Key Technical Concepts:
   - Build 0.3.310 (Android, posted Feb 11 in #builds) came off the EconomyChanges branch, whose head commit is Feb 6.
   - The economy line removed lives on Dec 3 (commit "Removed Lives and InfiniteLives references"). That makes the lives bugs Gone.
   - The economy line disabled Win & Collect on Dec 16 ("Disabled WinAndCollect"). That screen is switched off, so ENG-2424 stays open.
   - PR #1913 (Marcus/TileDozer_WindowFix) is open and unmerged, so it is not in the build.
   - PR #1916 (new camera config) was merged Dec 26 into EconomyChanges.
   - Other fix commits on the economy line:
     - "Fix for EndLevelPopup flickering on Tap Anywhere clicked" (Dec 5)
     - "Updated URLAudioPlayer to fully download clip if needed" (Dec 5)
     - "Nathan Animation Fix" (Dec 5)
     - "Fix issue opening Axe Arena panel from Nate Treasure button" (Dec 2)
